taxonomyNote: Animal Diversity Web and NAS list the older name Rana berlandieri; NatureServe notes three competing generic arrangements for American ranids and follows Nicholson (2025) in keeping Lithobates.
fieldMarks: Adults 5.7-11.4 cm snout-vent, a rather large leopard frog with an angular nose and long powerful legs (ADW; CDFW).
Gray, green or brown back with many irregular dark brown spots edged olive-green or light tan (ADW).
Prominent dorsolateral folds, usually pale yellow, that turn inward in front of the groin (ADW).
Cream belly fading to pale yellow on the upper thighs; females lighter and smaller than males (ADW).
behavior: Primarily nocturnal; chiefly a stream dweller that uses temporary and permanent water and is rarely far from it (NatureServe; CDFW; ADW).
Lays eggs after rains at almost any time of year, mostly March-May and August-November in Texas (NatureServe).
Males give mating trills, release calls and chuckle calls (ADW).
Disperses along canals, ditches and rivers (CDFW).
habitat: Streams, rivers, springs, stock ponds, backwaters, canals, ditches and arroyo pools in grassland, shrubland, savanna, desert and woodland; where introduced, mainly ditches, canals, irrigation sumps and modified rivers (NatureServe).
range: Native to extreme southern New Mexico and central and western Texas south through eastern and southern Mexico to Nicaragua; introduced and well established in the Imperial Valley and along the lower Colorado and Gila rivers in California and Arizona, replacing native lowland leopard frogs (NatureServe).
